name: Renderer Lifecycle
purpose: define renderer resolution, isolated loading/mounting, generation-safe commit, mount-instance cleanup and projector-boundary lifecycle semantics

resolution.default: renderer URL is derived from the base projector id
resolution.overrideBoundary: override must remain under /app/<projector-domain>/renderers/ and identify a .js module
mustNot: derive renderer path from DOM state
accept remote, query-bearing, fragment-bearing or traversal renderer URLs

destroy.scope: the single mount instance created by this mount call

mountSemantics.target: generation-isolated staging target owned by WebEngine and supplied to renderer mount
mountSemantics.commit: staging target is committed into the live boundary only after successful mount and only when that generation is still current
mountSemantics.projection: resolved projection input; renderer must not mutate it or become its authority
mountSemantics.context: frozen runtime/page/identity/access context plus projectorId and generation supplied by WebEngine
mountSemantics.instanceIsolation: each mount call is independent even when the same renderer module is mounted multiple times
mountSemantics.cleanupRule: cleanup is bound to the mount result of one mount call; module-global destroy state is not canonical

values.loading: WebEngine is loading or mounting the current projection generation
values.ready: the current generation mounted successfully and its staging target was committed with presentable output
values.empty: the current generation mounted successfully and its staging target was committed with no presentable output
values.denied: presentation was denied by authorization/preflight orchestration and no renderer mount is invoked for that generation
values.error: the current generation failed during renderer load or mount; the failure is isolated to this projector boundary
values.destroy: the previous/current generation has been invalidated and is being or has been torn down

rules: ready and empty are the only lifecycle outcomes a successful renderer mount may report
denied is owned by WebEngine authorization orchestration and is never returned by a renderer
error is produced by orchestration and is never used as a renderer success result
destroy is terminal for one mount generation even when the boundary is later reused
presentation state does not grant or revoke authorization
destroy -> loading is allowed only for a distinct new generation
error may be published by trusted WebEngine orchestration before renderer mount when a preflight dependency fails

asyncAndRaceSafety.generationRule: each mount attempt receives a monotonic boundary-local generation id
asyncAndRaceSafety.stagingRule: renderer writes occur against a generation-isolated staging target rather than the live boundary
asyncAndRaceSafety.lateCompletionRule: a superseded async generation is never committed into the live boundary
asyncAndRaceSafety.lateHandleRule: if a superseded mount later resolves with a destroy handle, WebEngine invokes that handle exactly once
asyncAndRaceSafety.cancellationRule: lifecycle correctness does not depend on renderer cancellation cooperation

when: page/surface owning the projection is destroyed
a superseded async mount later resolves
ordering: publish destroy for the old live generation when applicable
mark the old generation inactive so it cannot publish lifecycle state
remove renderer-owned live DOM from the boundary
invoke the returned mount-instance destroy handle exactly once when available
allow a distinct new generation to enter loading
destroySemantics.failureRule: destroy failure is reported diagnostically but contained to the old generation and cannot block or authorize a replacement generation

failureIsolation.loadOrMountFailure: current generation enters error and live renderer DOM is cleared
failureIsolation.staleFailure: failure from an obsolete generation cannot publish error over the current generation
failureIsolation.diagnostics: verbose failure details are emitted only through an optional diagnostic callback, never through shared presentation attributes

rules: renderers are executable implementations outside the projector tree
a renderer may use WebGUI, S3D or native browser capabilities
a renderer does not become the authority for domain data, authorization, SiteTree or Actions
the same renderer module may be mounted concurrently in multiple independent projection instances
a module-global destroy() that cannot identify a mount instance is not the canonical cleanup model
WebEngine owns lifecycle orchestration and state publication
UI lifecycle state is not an authoritative backend security boundary
